transition_sequences.window_duration_source: User observed the live POSTED-to-UNPOSTED transition; approximate duration.
transition_sequences.confidence: High for the UNPOSTED-to-POSTED transition; medium-high for the final UNPOSTED attribution because its URL is cropped. The approximately 10-second window is a user-observed estimate.

provisional_findings: Barrhaven and Ottawa show repeated UNPOSTED observations with the same job ID and same schedule ID.
St. Thomas shows the same job ID with one visible schedule in one observation and five visible schedules in another.
Barrhaven provides an ordered same-pair lifecycle: UNPOSTED at 7:45 PM, POSTED at 9:02 PM, then UNPOSTED again before 9:13 PM.
The user observed that the live POSTED state lasted approximately 10 seconds before returning to UNPOSTED.
Older competitor messages can have their POSTED/UNPOSTED labels removed by later edits, so a missing historical label is unknown rather than a negative status observation.
Hamilton YHM1 and Brampton YYZ4 each show one stable job ID associated with different schedule sets at different observations.
Brampton and Mississauga each contain multiple site codes with distinct stable job IDs; city alone is not a sufficient monitoring key.
Etobicoke also contains multiple site codes and distinct job IDs: DON9 with flexible delivery-station shifts and DTO3 with a full-time schedule.
Primary monitoring scope is Brampton, Mississauga, and Etobicoke; other sites remain valuable for session and state-transition tests.
The same job ID and schedule ID can survive a publication-status cycle; a status transition is more informative than a newly discovered identifier.
Telegram edited/display times have no visible date and cannot be ordered safely across screenshots.
A repeated or edited Telegram message is not proof that Amazon's postingStatus or capacity changed.
